investigations.name: island-biogeography
investigations.title: Island biogeography: a Lotka-Volterra metacommunity under contract
investigations.description:
A faithful process-bigraph port of vivarium-collective/island-biogeography
(experiments/island_lotka_volterra.py + experiments/island_food_web.py). Each
island is an IslandProcess running the discrete Lotka-Volterra step with a
carrying-capacity rescale; a single MigrationProcess couples them with
distance-stochastic single-individual migration and random species
introduction. Three studies interrogate the model against island-biogeography
theory: carrying-capacity scaling (area -> abundance), the isolation gradient
+ migration conservation, and the role of trophic structure in the
species-area law.
investigations.question:
Does the archived island-biogeography Lotka-Volterra metacommunity model,
faithfully ported into process-bigraph, reproduce the two central predictions
of MacArthur-Wilson island biogeography — species richness increasing with
island area and decreasing with isolation — and if not, what parts does it
reproduce and why?
investigations.hypothesis:
The model builds in the distance/isolation mechanism (migration_rate =
1/(1+distance)) and a per-island carrying capacity (area * individuals_per_area),
so we expect the immigration-distance gradient to hold robustly. The
area-richness law, however, is not built in: it must EMERGE from the
interaction dynamics, and we expect it to appear only when interactions are
trophic (a food web), not under random competition.
